The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	// This file holds the shared core of single-decision review. The online
2	// Store.RecheckDecision and the store-free RecheckDecisionOffline acquire
3	// their material differently — one reads an organization's live history
4	// and version snapshots, the other a chain-validated export paired with its
5	// separately retained checkpoint — but once the recorded request and the
6	// version it actually used are in hand, both replay the exact same
7	// judgment. That judgment lives only here so the two entry points can never
8	// drift on version-zero handling, envelope rejection order, or how a
9	// historical policy set is evaluated.
10	package darksafe
11	
12	// replayStatus reports whether replayRecordedDecision produced a decision
13	// or why the declared version could not be replayed.
14	type replayStatus int
15	
16	const (
17		// replayDecided means a Decision was recomputed.
18		replayDecided replayStatus = iota
19		// replayVersionAbsent means content for the declared version exists
20		// nowhere in the reviewer's material.
21		replayVersionAbsent
22		// replayVersionAfterTarget means the version's content exists, but only
23		// in a policy change record positioned after the reviewed decision.
24		// Online material never yields this: live version snapshots carry no
25		// position relative to audit records.
26		replayVersionAfterTarget
27	)
28	
29	// versionPolicies is one resolver verdict: either the detached full policy
30	// set of the requested version, or a status explaining why it is unusable.
31	type versionPolicies struct {
32		policies []Policy
33		status   replayStatus
34	}
35	
36	// resolveVersionPolicies supplies the full content of a non-zero version
37	// named by a reviewed decision. Implementations are responsible for
38	// detaching the returned policies from any state or input material.
39	type resolveVersionPolicies func(version int) versionPolicies
40	
41	// replayRecordedDecision re-judges a recorded request against the version
42	// the record declares it actually used. Later publishes or rollbacks are
43	// never substituted for that version.
44	//
45	// A version-0 record first replays the envelope rejections in their fixed
46	// order (missing organizations and identifiers, empty action, organization
47	// mismatch, illegal scope, disabled subject); a request that passes is the
48	// "organization has no published version" denial.
49	//
50	// For a non-zero record the version is resolved before any request rule is
51	// applied: a missing, or only-later, version is an error the caller turns
52	// into ErrVersionNotFound and must never be masked by an envelope denial,
53	// even for a disabled subject. Once the version is in hand, the same
54	// envelope checks run before policy evaluation, so a rejection reports
55	// version 0 with no matched policies regardless of what the version
56	// contains. Evaluation itself is the historical policy set only: deny
57	// overrides allow, matched identifiers are sorted, resource restrictions
58	// narrow rather than replace scope matching, and subject roles never stand
59	// in for an organization policy.
60	func replayRecordedDecision(org string, req OrgRequest, version int, resolve resolveVersionPolicies) (Decision, replayStatus) {
61		if version == 0 {
62			// The original evaluation used no published version: replay the
63			// envelope rejections exactly, in their recorded order, then the
64			// not-yet-published denial.
65			if d, ok := checkRequest(org, req); !ok {
66				return d, replayDecided
67			}
68			return Decision{Allowed: false, Reason: "organization has no published version"}, replayDecided
69		}
70		// Resolve the version first. A request the envelope would reject must
71		// not turn a missing or later-only declared version into an ordinary
72		// denial.
73		resolved := resolve(version)
74		if resolved.status != replayDecided {
75			return Decision{}, resolved.status
76		}
77		// The version exists as claimed, but chain integrity does not imply the
78		// request was admissible: re-run the same envelope checks the online
79		// decision runs before any policy is consulted. A rejection here
80		// evaluates no policies, hence version 0 and no matches, even when the
81		// version holds a fully matching allow policy.
82		if d, ok := checkRequest(org, req); !ok {
83			return d, replayDecided
84		}
85		return evaluate(req, resolved.policies, version), replayDecided
86	}

1	// This file implements offline review of a single audited decision. It
2	// works solely from exported audit material: the complete record export,
3	// the separately retained checkpoint, and a target sequence. No Store is
4	// created or restored, so an organization can confirm why an access was
5	// allowed or denied long after the service instance that decided it has
6	// ended.
7	//
8	// The complete input must first validate as an audit chain. The policy
9	// version a decision actually used is recovered exclusively from policy
10	// change records preceding that decision within the same organization's
11	// export; later publishes or rollbacks, and a wider later export, cannot
12	// change the recomputed result.
13	package darksafe
14	
15	import "fmt"
16	
17	// OfflineDecisionReview compares the decision stored in an audited record
18	// with a decision recomputed purely from the exported material.
19	type OfflineDecisionReview struct {
20		// Seq is the reviewed decision record's sequence.
21		Seq int
22		// Original is the decision preserved in the audited record.
23		Original Decision
24		// Recomputed is the decision evaluated again offline from the saved
25		// request and the policy version it originally used.
26		Recomputed Decision
27		// Consistent reports whether both decisions agree on every field
28		// (allowance, reason, matched policies and version), treating a nil
29		// matched list and an empty matched list as the same.
30		Consistent bool
31	}
32	
33	// RecheckDecisionOffline re-evaluates one decision record offline. org is
34	// the organization name, records is its complete export starting at
35	// sequence 1 (a valid prefix is sufficient when paired with its own
36	// checkpoint), cp is the separately saved checkpoint, and seq identifies
37	// the decision record to review. The call is read-only: it neither mutates
38	// the supplied material nor appends audit records, and the returned
39	// decisions are detached from the input slices.
40	//
41	// The entire export is chain-validated before any result is produced;
42	// tampering anywhere, including in records after the target, fails the
43	// review. Distinguishable errors follow the other audit entry points:
44	// ErrMissingOrganization for an empty organization, ErrAuditNotFound for a
45	// non-positive or absent target sequence, and ErrAuditNotADecision when the
46	// target is a policy change record. When the saved decision names a
47	// policy version whose full content has no change record before the
48	// target, ErrVersionNotFound is returned; a newer version is never
49	// substituted, and a request the envelope would reject never masks the
50	// missing version.
51	//
52	// The fingerprint only proves the material matches its checkpoint; it
53	// cannot stand in for evaluating the request itself. So even when the
54	// declared version exists and carries an otherwise matching allow policy,
55	// the recomputation enforces the same request rules as the online
56	// decision: a disabled subject, an organization mismatch, a missing
57	// subject or resource organization or identifier, an empty action, and an
58	// illegal resource scope all deny, with the same reasons and precedence as
59	// Decide. Such a rejection uses no policies, so the recomputed decision
60	// reports version 0 with no matched policies; it is then compared field by
61	// field with the preserved original and may come back inconsistent.
62	func RecheckDecisionOffline(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint, seq int) (OfflineDecisionReview, error) {
63		if org == "" {
64			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, ErrMissingOrganization
65		}
66		// Validate the whole export first. A subject-filtered page, a fragment
67		// missing the beginning, or a checkpoint that does not pin the records
68		// all fail here, as does any corruption after the target.
69		if err := VerifyAudit(org, records, cp); err != nil {
70			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, err
71		}
72		if seq < 1 {
73			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, seq)
74		}
75		if seq > len(records) {
76			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: export ends at %d, no sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, len(records), seq)
77		}
78		rec := &records[seq-1]
79		if rec.Kind != AuditDecision || rec.Decision == nil {
80			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d is %s", ErrAuditNotADecision, seq, rec.Kind)
81		}
82	
83		original := cloneDecisionValue(rec.Decision.Decision)
84		req := rec.Decision.Request
85		// Detach the request list by non-nil rather than by length: a non-nil
86		// empty role list with spare capacity must not be shared back with the
87		// caller's material, even though evaluation never reads any element.
88		req.Subject.Roles = cloneStrings(req.Subject.Roles)
89		version := original.Version
90	
91		// The version's full content must travel in a same-organization policy
92		// change record positioned before the decision. The replay core resolves
93		// the version before replaying any request rule, so a request the
94		// envelope rejects cannot mask a missing or later-only version.
95		resolve := func(want int) versionPolicies {
96			if policies, found := policiesBefore(records, seq-1, want); found {
97				return versionPolicies{policies: policies}
98			}
99			if _, later := policiesBefore(records, len(records), want); later {
100				return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAfterTarget}
101			}
102			return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAbsent}
103		}
104		recomputed, status := replayRecordedDecision(org, req, version, resolve)
105		switch status {
106		case replayVersionAfterTarget:
107			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf(
108				"%w: decision at sequence %d used version %d, whose change record appears only after it",
109				ErrVersionNotFound, seq, version)
110		case replayVersionAbsent:
111			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf(
112				"%w: decision at sequence %d used version %d, which has no policy change record in the export",
113				ErrVersionNotFound, seq, version)
114		}
115	
116		return OfflineDecisionReview{
117			Seq:        seq,
118			Original:   original,
119			Recomputed: recomputed,
120			Consistent: decisionsEqual(original, recomputed),
121		}, nil
122	}
123	
124	// policiesBefore searches records[:limit] for the policy change record that
125	// published version and returns a detached copy of its full content. The
126	// gapless chain validation guarantees records are in sequence order.
127	func policiesBefore(records []AuditRecord, limit, version int) ([]Policy, bool) {
128		for i := 0; i < limit; i++ {
129			r := &records[i]
130			if r.Kind != AuditPolicyChange || r.Change == nil {
131				continue
132			}
133			if r.Change.Version == version {
134				return append([]Policy(nil), r.Change.Policies...), true
135			}
136		}
137		return nil, false
138	}
139	
140	// cloneDecisionValue returns a decision detached from the input's matched
141	// slice. The list is detached whenever it is non-nil, including a non-nil
142	// empty list that still has spare capacity, so an append by one receiver
143	// can never reach another copy.
144	func cloneDecisionValue(d Decision) Decision {
145		d.Matched = cloneStrings(d.Matched)
146		return d
147	}
148	
149	// decisionsEqual compares every decision field. A nil matched list and an
150	// empty matched list describe the same set of hits.
151	func decisionsEqual(a, b Decision) bool {
152		if a.Allowed != b.Allowed || a.Reason != b.Reason || a.Version != b.Version {
153			return false
154		}
155		if len(a.Matched) == 0 && len(b.Matched) == 0 {
156			return true
157		}
158		if len(a.Matched) != len(b.Matched) {
159			return false
160		}
161		for i := range a.Matched {
162			if a.Matched[i] != b.Matched[i] {
163				return false
164			}
165		}
166		return true
167	}

1	// The review subcommand re-evaluates one decision preserved in an audit
2	// archive after the service instance that decided it has ended. It never
3	// talks to a running service and never creates or restores a Store: the
4	// decision is recomputed purely from the saved record's request, the
5	// historical policy version carried in records before it, and a checkpoint
6	// the caller retained separately from the archive.
7	package main
8	
9	import (
10		"errors"
11		"fmt"
12		"io"
13		"os"
14		"strconv"
15		"strings"
16	
17		"github.com/asdhoaiqqq/darksafe-access/darksafe"
18	)
19	
20	// Exit codes for the review command:
21	//
22	//   - 0: a full review was produced and the complete report was written
23	//     without error, including a legitimate archive whose original and
24	//     recomputed decisions disagree.
25	//   - 2: the invocation itself is wrong (missing/invalid arguments, the
26	//     archive file cannot be read).
27	//   - 1: the material or target cannot support a review (an invalid or
28	//     chain-broken archive, a missing or non-decision target, a historical
29	//     policy version that cannot be obtained), or the review report could
30	//     not be written out in full.
31	const (
32		reviewExitOK     = 0
33		reviewExitFailed = 1
34		reviewExitUsage  = 2
35	)
36	
37	// reviewInputs holds everything the review command needs from the caller.
38	type reviewInputs struct {
39		archivePath string
40		org         string
41		seq         int
42		endSeq      int
43		fingerprint string
44		// json selects machine-readable JSON output instead of the default text
45		// report. The review itself is identical either way: the same archive
46		// validation and the same historical recheck, never a re-submitted
47		// request.
48		json bool
49	}
50	
51	func reviewHelp(w io.Writer) {
52		fmt.Fprint(w, `usage: darksafe review --archive FILE --org ORG --seq N \
53	                      --end-seq N --fingerprint HEX
54	
55	Review one access decision saved in an audit archive, long after the
56	service instance that made the decision has ended. No running service is
57	contacted and no policy store is created or restored; the decision is
58	recomputed offline from the archived material alone. The archived decision
59	is never re-submitted as a new access request.
60	
61	Required inputs:
62	  --archive FILE       path to the audit archive written by
63	                       EncodeAuditArchive (the complete export, not a
64	                       subject-filtered page or a fragment)
65	  --org ORG            organization name the archive belongs to; it must
66	                       match the organization bound into the records
67	  --seq N              positive sequence number of the decision record to
68	                       review (organization-local, starting at 1)
69	  --end-seq N          end sequence of the checkpoint retained separately
70	                       from the archive (0 for an organization with no
71	                       records); must not be negative
72	  --fingerprint HEX    checkpoint fingerprint retained separately from the
73	                       archive (64 hexadecimal SHA-256 characters)
74	  --json               emit the review as one complete JSON object on
75	                       stdout instead of the text report. The object gives
76	                       "target_sequence", "original" and "recomputed"
77	                       decisions (each with "allowed", "reason",
78	                       "matched_policies" in original order, and
79	                       "policy_version"), and "consistent". A valid UTF-8
80	                       string is a JSON string; a string that is not valid
81	                       UTF-8 is the object {"base64": "<standard base64 of
82	                       the exact bytes>"}, so a lone 0xFF, a lone 0xFE and a
83	                       real U+FFFD never collapse together and every string's
84	                       original bytes can be recovered. A nil and an empty
85	                       matched list both render as []. A failure before the
86	                       report is written leaves stdout empty and the reason on
87	                       stderr only; if stdout refuses the report or accepts
88	                       only part of it, any accepted prefix stays in place,
89	                       the command exits 1 and the output failure is reported
90	                       on stderr, never retried in another format.
91	
92	The checkpoint carried inside the archive is informational only: validation
93	always uses --end-seq/--fingerprint supplied here. Even when --seq points at
94	an early record, every archived record is checked; a corrupted or missing
95	later record, or any mismatch with the retained checkpoint, fails the whole
96	review with no partial output.
97	
98	The request is replayed strictly against the policy version the recorded
99	decision actually used; later publishes or rollbacks present in the archive
100	are never substituted. A chain that is valid but whose original and
101	recomputed decisions disagree is still printed in full and exits 0; the
102	disagreement is shown explicitly rather than reported as file damage.
103	
104	Strings may contain spaces, control characters or non-UTF-8 bytes; the text
105	report uses Go-style quoting, while --json uses the JSON string /
106	{"base64": ...} rule described above, and both keep different raw bytes
107	distinguishable. This command only reads the named archive: it neither
108	rewrites it nor appends audit records.
109	
110	Exit codes: 0 complete report written without error (decisions may
111	disagree), 1 archive or target invalid / historical version unavailable /
112	review report could not be written out in full, 2 bad arguments or
113	unreadable file. --json changes none of these.
114	
115	Example:
116	  (materials produced by examples/offline_review; seq 1 is the
117	  policy publish record, seq 2 is the read decision being reviewed)
118	  darksafe review --archive acme-factory.audit \
119	      --org 'acme factory' --seq 2 --end-seq 2 \
120	      --fingerprint 04b274dbb4cf039bbb4b78f5ee5aae03278d2c34833fe87fecb13ade51ef5299
121	
122	  add --json to get the same review as one JSON object:
123	  darksafe review --json --archive acme-factory.audit \
124	      --org 'acme factory' --seq 2 --end-seq 2 \
125	      --fingerprint 04b274dbb4cf039bbb4b78f5ee5aae03278d2c34833fe87fecb13ade51ef5299
126	`)
127	}
128	
129	// parseReviewArgs parses review arguments. flags is an injectable args slice
130	// so tests can drive the command directly. The first element of args is the
131	// subcommand name ("review"). --help/-h/-help set wantHelp.
132	func parseReviewArgs(args []string) (in reviewInputs, wantHelp bool, err error) {
133		haveSeq, haveEndSeq := false, false
134		for i := 1; i < len(args); i++ {
135			arg := args[i]
136			value := ""
137			hasValue := false
138			switch {
139			case arg == "--help" || arg == "-h" || arg == "-help":
140				return reviewInputs{}, true, nil
141			case len(arg) > 2 && arg[:2] == "--":
142				// Accept both --flag value and --flag=value.
143				if eq := strings.IndexByte(arg, '='); eq >= 0 {
144					value = arg[eq+1:]
145					hasValue = true
146					arg = arg[:eq]
147				}
148			default:
149				return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("unexpected argument %q", arg)
150			}
151	
152			take := func() (string, error) {
153				if hasValue {
154					return value, nil
155				}
156				if i+1 >= len(args) {
157					return "", fmt.Errorf("flag %s requires a value", arg)
158				}
159				i++
160				return args[i], nil
161			}
162	
163			switch arg {
164			case "--archive":
165				v, err := take()
166				if err != nil {
167					return reviewInputs{}, false, err
168				}
169				in.archivePath = v
170			case "--org":
171				v, err := take()
172				if err != nil {
173					return reviewInputs{}, false, err
174				}
175				in.org = v
176			case "--seq":
177				v, err := take()
178				if err != nil {
179					return reviewInputs{}, false, err
180				}
181				n, perr := strconv.Atoi(v)
182				if perr != nil {
183					return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("--seq must be an integer, got %q", v)
184				}
185				in.seq = n
186				haveSeq = true
187			case "--end-seq":
188				v, err := take()
189				if err != nil {
190					return reviewInputs{}, false, err
191				}
192				n, perr := strconv.Atoi(v)
193				if perr != nil {
194					return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("--end-seq must be an integer, got %q", v)
195				}
196				in.endSeq = n
197				haveEndSeq = true
198			case "--fingerprint":
199				v, err := take()
200				if err != nil {
201					return reviewInputs{}, false, err
202				}
203				in.fingerprint = v
204			case "--json":
205				// Bare --json enables JSON output; --json=value accepts the
206				// usual boolean spellings. No value is ever consumed from the
207				// following token, so "--json --seq 2" keeps working.
208				switch {
209				case !hasValue:
210					in.json = true
211				default:
212					b, perr := strconv.ParseBool(value)
213					if perr != nil {
214						return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("--json must be a boolean, got %q", value)
215					}
216					in.json = b
217				}
218			default:
219				return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("unknown review flag %q", arg)
220			}
221		}
222	
223		if in.archivePath == "" {
224			return reviewInputs{}, false, errors.New("--archive is required")
225		}
226		if in.org == "" {
227			return reviewInputs{}, false, errors.New("--org is required")
228		}
229		if !haveSeq {
230			return reviewInputs{}, false, errors.New("--seq is required")
231		}
232		if in.seq <= 0 {
233			return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("--seq must be a positive integer, got %d", in.seq)
234		}
235		if !haveEndSeq {
236			return reviewInputs{}, false, errors.New("--end-seq is required")
237		}
238		if in.endSeq < 0 {
239			return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("--end-seq must not be negative, got %d", in.endSeq)
240		}
241		if in.fingerprint == "" {
242			return reviewInputs{}, false, errors.New("--fingerprint is required")
243		}
244		return in, false, nil
245	}
246	
247	// runReview executes one offline review and returns the process exit code.
248	// stdout/stderr are injectable so the command stays testable; args is the
249	// full argument vector including the leading "review".
250	func runReview(args []string, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int {
251		in, wantHelp, err := parseReviewArgs(args)
252		if wantHelp {
253			reviewHelp(stdout)
254			return reviewExitOK
255		}
256		if err != nil {
257			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: %s\n", err)
258			return reviewExitUsage
259		}
260	
261		archive, err := os.ReadFile(in.archivePath)
262		if err != nil {
263			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: cannot read archive %q: %v\n", in.archivePath, err)
264			return reviewExitUsage
265		}
266	
267		cp := darksafe.Checkpoint{Org: in.org, EndSeq: in.endSeq, Fingerprint: in.fingerprint}
268		records, err := darksafe.DecodeAuditArchive(archive, in.org, cp)
269		if err != nil {
270			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: archive validation failed: %v\n", err)
271			return reviewExitFailed
272		}
273		review, err := darksafe.RecheckDecisionOffline(in.org, records, cp, in.seq)
274		if err != nil {
275			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: %v\n", err)
276			return reviewExitFailed
277		}
278	
279		// Render both formats fully before touching stdout: a render failure must
280		// not leave partial output, and every earlier failure path already
281		// returned with stdout untouched.
282		var payload []byte
283		if in.json {
284			payload, err = renderReviewJSON(review)
285			if err != nil {
286				fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: cannot encode result as JSON: %v\n", err)
287				return reviewExitFailed
288			}
289		} else {
290			var buf strings.Builder
291			printReview(&buf, review)
292			payload = []byte(buf.String())
293		}
294	
295		// Success requires the WHOLE report to actually land. A receiver may
296		// accept some bytes and then refuse the rest, or report a short write
297		// with no error; neither may be mistaken for a completed review merely
298		// because the archive validated and the decision recomputed. Whatever
299		// prefix the receiver already accepted stays there (it cannot be
300		// unwritten), but nothing more is appended afterwards.
301		n, werr := stdout.Write(payload)
302		if werr != nil {
303			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: failed to write review report: %v\n", werr)
304			return reviewExitFailed
305		}
306		if n < len(payload) {
307			fmt.Fprintf(stderr,
308				"review: review report output incomplete: wrote %d of %d bytes\n",
309				n, len(payload))
310			return reviewExitFailed
311		}
312		return reviewExitOK
313	}
314	
315	// printReview renders the target sequence, both full decisions and the
316	// consistency verdict. Every potentially non-UTF-8 string is emitted with
317	// %q (Go quoting): a lone 0xFF renders as "\xff", 0xFE as "\xfe" and a real
318	// U+FFFD as "�", so distinct raw bytes never collapse onto one glyph.
319	func printReview(w io.Writer, r darksafe.OfflineDecisionReview) {
320		fmt.Fprintf(w, "target sequence: %d\n", r.Seq)
321		fmt.Fprintln(w, "original decision:")
322		printDecision(w, r.Original)
323		fmt.Fprintln(w, "recomputed decision:")
324		printDecision(w, r.Recomputed)
325		if r.Consistent {
326			fmt.Fprintln(w, "consistent: yes")
327		} else {
328			fmt.Fprintln(w, "consistent: no (original and recomputed decisions differ)")
329		}
330	}
331	
332	func printDecision(w io.Writer, d darksafe.Decision) {
333		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  allowed: %v\n", d.Allowed)
334		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  reason: %q\n", d.Reason)
335		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  matched policies: %s\n", formatMatched(d.Matched))
336		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  policy version: %d\n", d.Version)
337	}
338	
339	// formatMatched quotes each matched policy identifier byte-for-byte. A nil
340	// and an empty list mean the same set of hits but keep distinguishable
341	// spellings, mirroring the library's own nil-versus-empty preservation.
342	func formatMatched(matched []string) string {
343		if matched == nil {
344			return "[]"
345		}
346		out := "["
347		for i, id := range matched {
348			if i > 0 {
349				out += ", "
350			}
351			out += strconv.Quote(id)
352		}
353		return out + "]"
354	}

README.md:308:`review` 子命令在原服务实例结束后，仅凭一份保存的审计归档复核其中**一条已有访问决策**，不联系运行中的服务，也不创建或恢复策略存储，更不会把该决策的请求重新提交。它顺序调用 `DecodeAuditArchive` 与 `RecheckDecisionOffline`：先按另行保留的检查点校验整份材料，再用决策记录里保存的请求与其实际使用的历史策略版本重算。
README.md:334:加上 `--json` 后，复核过程完全不变（仍然先 `DecodeAuditArchive` 全量链校验、再 `RecheckDecisionOffline` 按当时版本重算，不重新提交访问请求、不改用较新策略、不改写归档、不追加审计记录），只是标准输出变成**且仅变成**一份完整的 JSON 对象：没有标题、说明，也不混入文字版报告。归档、目标或历史版本方面的失败（退出码 1）与参数/文件失败（退出码 2）都发生在报告开始写出之前，标准输出保持为空，原因只写标准错误；即使目标序号靠前，只要归档后面的记录损坏，整次失败且不交付部分 JSON。若标准输出接收方拒绝写入或只接收部分字节（即使没有同时返回错误），已接收的前缀原样保留、不撤回，但以退出码 1 结束并在标准错误说明复核报告输出失败，此后不再追加内容、也不退回文字格式补写——因此只有完整对象无错误写出时退出码才是 0。

1	// This file implements lossless archiving of one organization's audit
2	// export. AuditExport hands back detached in-memory records and the caller
3	// separately retains the checkpoint pinning them; an archive serializes the
4	// export so it can be saved to a file when the service instance ends and
5	// read back later, still paired with the caller's own checkpoint and still
6	// usable as the material for RecheckDecisionOffline.
7	//
8	// The format is a length-delimited binary encoding built by hand rather
9	// than encoding/json: JSON text cannot carry bytes that are not valid
10	// UTF-8 without silently replacing them with U+FFFD, which would collapse
11	// genuinely different content (a lone 0xFF, a lone 0xFE and a real U+FFFD)
12	// onto identical records and change their fingerprints. Every string is
13	// written from its exact bytes with a length prefix, and nil slices,
14	// non-nil empty slices and absent payloads are each marked explicitly.
15	//
16	// Integrity never comes from trust in the file. A decode reconstructs the
17	// records and then runs the same whole-material VerifyAudit chain check
18	// against the checkpoint the caller supplies independently; the checkpoint
19	// embedded in the archive is informational only and never authoritative.
20	package darksafe
21	
22	import (
23		"bytes"
24		"crypto/sha256"
25		"encoding/binary"
26		"errors"
27		"fmt"
28	)
29	
30	// ErrInvalidArchive means archive bytes are not a recognizable, complete,
31	// untampered audit archive: a foreign/truncated/trailing-byte framing, a
32	// failed checksum, or content that does not decode. Content-level failures
33	// (missing or mismatched organization, missing, out-of-order or modified
34	// records, a mismatched checkpoint) keep using ErrMissingOrganization and
35	// ErrInvalidRange exactly as the other audit entry points do.
36	var ErrInvalidArchive = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit archive")
37	
38	// Archive framing:
39	//
40	//	magic   = archiveMagic
41	//	u32 BE  = byte length of the payload that follows
42	//	payload = archivePayloadLen bytes
43	//	32 bytes = SHA-256 checksum of payload
44	//
45	// A second archive concatenated to a first is trailing material, not a
46	// second frame: a read consumes exactly one frame and rejects any byte
47	// beyond it.
48	const archiveMagic = "darksafe-audit-archive-v1\n"
49	
50	const (
51		archiveTagBoolFalse byte = 0
52		archiveTagBoolTrue  byte = 1
53		archiveTagNil       byte = 0
54		archiveTagPresent   byte = 1
55	)
56	
57	// archiveWriter appends length-delimited fields to a byte buffer.
58	type archiveWriter struct {
59		buf []byte
60		err error
61	}
62	
63	func (w *archiveWriter) raw(data []byte) {
64		w.buf = append(w.buf, data...)
65	}
66	
67	// u32 writes a non-negative int as a big-endian uint32.
68	func (w *archiveWriter) u32(v int) {
69		if v < 0 || uint64(v) > 0xffffffff {
70			w.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: length out of range: %d", ErrInvalidArchive, v)
71			return
72		}
73		var b [4]byte
74		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(v))
75		w.buf = append(w.buf, b[:]...)
76	}
77	
78	func (w *archiveWriter) boolean(v bool) {
79		if v {
80			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagBoolTrue)
81		} else {
82			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagBoolFalse)
83		}
84	}
85	
86	// put appends one raw framing byte. It is the archive sink's side of the
87	// shared list shape: the list presence marker (archiveTagNil for nil,
88	// archiveTagPresent for a non-nil list) goes into the payload verbatim.
89	func (w *archiveWriter) put(b byte) {
90		w.buf = append(w.buf, b)
91	}
92	
93	// listCount writes a list element count through the archive's own
94	// range-checked u32, so a list length the uint32 format cannot represent
95	// still fails the whole archive with the existing ErrInvalidArchive rather
96	// than emitting truncated framing or returning partial bytes.
97	func (w *archiveWriter) listCount(n int) {
98		w.u32(n)
99	}
100	
101	// stringField writes a string from its exact memory bytes. Nothing is
102	// validated, replaced or normalized: a lone 0xFF reaches the output as
103	// itself and stays distinguishable from 0xFE and a genuine U+FFFD.
104	func (w *archiveWriter) stringField(s string) {
105		w.u32(len(s))
106		if w.err != nil {
107			return
108		}
109		w.buf = append(w.buf, s...)
110	}
111	
112	// policy writes one Policy by walking the single policy field table, so the
113	// archive's field order is the fingerprint's order by construction. Even the
114	// fingerprint-optional ResourceID is always written here (empty included),
115	// so every field round trips on its own; its placement is fixed by the
116	// table and therefore cannot move a fingerprint boundary.
117	func (w *archiveWriter) policy(p Policy) {
118		for i := range policyFields {
119			f := &policyFields[i]
120			switch f.kind {
121			case policyFieldString, policyFieldOptionalString:
122				w.stringField(f.getString(p))
123			case policyFieldBool:
124				w.boolean(f.getBool(p))
125			}
126		}
127	}
128	
129	// change writes the policy-change payload, or a single absence marker:
130	// VerifyAudit only ever accepts a change payload on a policy-change record
131	// and its absence otherwise, but the distinction is encoded explicitly so
132	// decode never has to reconstruct a shape. A present payload walks the
133	// single policy-change field table, so the archive's field order is the
134	// fingerprint's order by construction and every change field round trips.
135	func (w *archiveWriter) change(c *PolicyChange) {
136		if c == nil {
137			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagNil)
138			return
139		}
140		w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagPresent)
141		for i := range changeFields {
142			f := &changeFields[i]
143			switch f.kind {
144			case changeFieldInt:
145				w.u32(f.getInt(c))
146			case changeFieldPolicyList:
147				writeListShape(w, f.getPolicies(c), w.policy)
148			case changeFieldBool:
149				w.boolean(f.getBool(c))
150			}
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// decisionRecord writes the decision payload, or a single absence marker:
155	// VerifyAudit only ever accepts a decision payload on a decision record and
156	// its absence otherwise, but the distinction is encoded explicitly so decode
157	// never has to reconstruct a shape. A present payload walks the single
158	// decision field table, so the archive's field order is the fingerprint's
159	// order by construction and every request and decision field round trips.
160	func (w *archiveWriter) decisionRecord(d *DecisionRecord) {
161		if d == nil {
162			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagNil)
163			return
164		}
165		w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagPresent)
166		for i := range decisionFields {
167			f := &decisionFields[i]
168			switch f.kind {
169			case decisionFieldString:
170				w.stringField(f.getString(d))
171			case decisionFieldStringList:
172				writeListShape(w, f.getList(d), w.stringField)
173			case decisionFieldBool:
174				w.boolean(f.getBool(d))
175			case decisionFieldInt:
176				w.u32(f.getInt(d))
177			}
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// EncodeAuditArchive serializes one complete audit export into savable
182	// bytes. org is the organization name, records is its complete chain from
183	// sequence 1 (a valid prefix ending at some historical sequence is enough,
184	// provided cp pins exactly that sequence), and cp is the checkpoint the
185	// caller separately retains. An organization with no records archives too:
186	// records is empty and cp is its sequence-0 genesis checkpoint.
187	//
188	// The whole material is validated exactly as VerifyAudit would before any
189	// bytes are returned: a missing organization is ErrMissingOrganization, and
190	// a missing, out-of-order or foreign record, modified content or checkpoint
191	// mismatch is ErrInvalidRange. On failure no archive bytes are returned.
192	// The checkpoint is carried in the archive for reference, but never stands
193	// in for the separately retained evidence: DecodeAuditArchive always
194	// validates against the checkpoint handed to it. The call is read-only:
195	// neither the records nor any service state are mutated and no audit record
196	// is appended.
197	func EncodeAuditArchive(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint) ([]byte, error) {
198		if org == "" {
199			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
200		}
201		if err := VerifyAudit(org, records, cp); err != nil {
202			return nil, err
203		}
204	
205		pw := &archiveWriter{}
206		pw.stringField(org)
207		pw.u32(cp.EndSeq)
208		pw.stringField(cp.Fingerprint)
209		pw.u32(len(records))
210		for i := range records {
211			rec := &records[i]
212			// The outer record fields walk the single record field table, so
213			// the archive's record layout is the fingerprint envelope's layout
214			// — plus the record's own fingerprint, which the envelope excludes
215			// — by construction, and no outer field can be skipped or
216			// reordered here alone.
217			for j := range recordFields {
218				f := &recordFields[j]
219				switch f.kind {
220				case recordFieldString:
221					pw.stringField(f.getString(rec))
222				case recordFieldInt:
223					pw.u32(f.getInt(rec))
224				case recordFieldChange:
225					pw.change(f.getChange(rec))
226				case recordFieldDecision:
227					pw.decisionRecord(f.getDecision(rec))
228				}
229			}
230		}
231		if pw.err != nil {
232			return nil, pw.err
233		}
234		payload := pw.buf
235	
236		out := make([]byte, 0, len(archiveMagic)+4+len(payload)+sha256.Size)
237		out = append(out, archiveMagic...)
238		var lenBuf [4]byte
239		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(lenBuf[:], uint32(len(payload)))
240		out = append(out, lenBuf[:]...)
241		out = append(out, payload...)
242		sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
243		out = append(out, sum[:]...)
244		return out, nil
245	}
246	
247	// archiveReader walks one payload without copying string contents: string
248	// fields are backed by the payload slice itself, which is owned by the
249	// decoder and never returned, so callers cannot mutate the input through
250	// the result.
251	type archiveReader struct {
252		data []byte
253		pos  int
254		err  error
255	}
256	
257	func (r *archiveReader) need(n int) bool {
258		if r.err != nil {
259			return false
260		}
261		if n < 0 || r.pos > len(r.data)-n {
262			r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: truncated archive payload", ErrInvalidArchive)
263			return false
264		}
265		return true
266	}
267	
268	func (r *archiveReader) marker() byte {
269		if !r.need(1) {
270			return 0
271		}
272		b := r.data[r.pos]
273		r.pos++
274		return b
275	}
276	
277	func (r *archiveReader) u32() int {
278		if !r.need(4) {
279			return 0
280		}
281		v := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(r.data[r.pos : r.pos+4]))
282		r.pos += 4
283		return v
284	}
285	
286	// boundedCount reads a count and proves at least minBytesPerItem bytes
287	// remain per item, so a hostile payload cannot drive a huge allocation
288	// with a count its body could never satisfy.
289	func (r *archiveReader) boundedCount(minBytesPerItem int) int {
290		n := r.u32()
291		if r.err != nil {
292			return 0
293		}
294		if n < 0 || uint64(n)*uint64(minBytesPerItem) > uint64(len(r.data)-r.pos) {
295			r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: implausible list count %d", ErrInvalidArchive, n)
296			return 0
297		}
298		return n
299	}
300	
301	func (r *archiveReader) boolean() bool {
302		switch r.marker() {
303		case archiveTagBoolTrue:
304			return true
305		case archiveTagBoolFalse:
306			return false
307		default:
308			if r.err == nil {
309				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid boolean marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
310			}
311			return false
312		}
313	}
314	
315	func (r *archiveReader) stringField() string {
316		n := r.u32()
317		if r.err != nil {
318			return ""
319		}
320		if !r.need(n) {
321			return ""
322		}
323		// Conversion copies the bytes, so the result never aliases the input.
324		s := string(r.data[r.pos : r.pos+n])
325		r.pos += n
326		return s
327	}
328	
329	// readList reads one length-counted list framed by writeListShape on the
330	// archive sink, whatever its item type: both string lists and the policy
331	// list decode here. Every list
332	// kind gets the exact same framing checks — the nil/presence marker, the
333	// per-item byte floor before any allocation, and each item's own
334	// truncation/structure errors — so a hostile count can neither drive a
335	// disproportionate allocation nor deliver a partial list: once an item
336	// fails, the reader's sticky error fails the whole read.
337	// minBytesPerItem is the minimum an item could occupy (each string item
338	// carries one length word; a policy item carries six length words and a
339	// bool), and is used only to reject counts the remaining bytes could never
340	// satisfy.
341	func readList[T any](r *archiveReader, minBytesPerItem int, readItem func() T) []T {
342		switch r.marker() {
343		case archiveTagNil:
344			return nil
345		case archiveTagPresent:
346		default:
347			if r.err == nil {
348				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid list marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
349			}
350			return nil
351		}
352		n := r.boundedCount(minBytesPerItem)
353		if r.err != nil {
354			return nil
355		}
356		items := make([]T, n)
357		for i := range items {
358			items[i] = readItem()
359		}
360		return items
361	}
362	
363	func (r *archiveReader) policy() Policy {
364		// Read fields in the single table's (write and fingerprint) order. The
365		// fingerprint-optional ResourceID is still a mandatory, fixed field on
366		// the archive, so it is read for every policy including the empty one.
367		var p Policy
368		for i := range policyFields {
369			f := &policyFields[i]
370			switch f.kind {
371			case policyFieldString, policyFieldOptionalString:
372				f.setString(&p, r.stringField())
373			case policyFieldBool:
374				f.setBool(&p, r.boolean())
375			}
376		}
377		return p
378	}
379	
380	func (r *archiveReader) change() *PolicyChange {
381		switch r.marker() {
382		case archiveTagNil:
383			return nil
384		case archiveTagPresent:
385		default:
386			if r.err == nil {
387				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid change payload marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
388			}
389			return nil
390		}
391		// Read fields in the single table's (write and fingerprint) order, so a
392		// field can never be restored into the wrong member or skipped.
393		c := &PolicyChange{}
394		for i := range changeFields {
395			f := &changeFields[i]
396			switch f.kind {
397			case changeFieldInt:
398				f.setInt(c, r.u32())
399			case changeFieldPolicyList:
400				// A policy writes six length words (five strings plus
401				// ResourceID) and one bool byte at minimum.
402				f.setPolicies(c, readList(r, 6*4+1, r.policy))
403			case changeFieldBool:
404				f.setBool(c, r.boolean())
405			}
406		}
407		return c
408	}
409	
410	func (r *archiveReader) decisionRecord() *DecisionRecord {
411		switch r.marker() {
412		case archiveTagNil:
413			return nil
414		case archiveTagPresent:
415		default:
416			if r.err == nil {
417				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid decision payload marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
418			}
419			return nil
420		}
421		// Read fields in the single table's (write and fingerprint) order, so a
422		// field can never be restored into the wrong member or skipped.
423		d := &DecisionRecord{}
424		for i := range decisionFields {
425			f := &decisionFields[i]
426			switch f.kind {
427			case decisionFieldString:
428				f.setString(d, r.stringField())
429			case decisionFieldStringList:
430				// Each string item carries at least one length word.
431				f.setList(d, readList(r, 4, r.stringField))
432			case decisionFieldBool:
433				f.setBool(d, r.boolean())
434			case decisionFieldInt:
435				f.setInt(d, r.u32())
436			}
437		}
438		return d
439	}
440	
441	// DecodeAuditArchive reads one archive produced by EncodeAuditArchive and
442	// returns records that can be handed directly to RecheckDecisionOffline.
443	// org is the organization the caller expects, and cp is the checkpoint the
444	// caller independently retained; the checkpoint embedded in the file is
445	// never treated as evidence, so even an archive carrying a plausible
446	// checkpoint only validates against the one supplied here.
447	//
448	// A missing organization is ErrMissingOrganization. Unrecognized framing,
449	// truncation, a trailing second archive or any other extra byte, a bad
450	// checksum, and undecodable content are ErrInvalidArchive. Records that
451	// decode but are missing, out of order, foreign to the organization,
452	// modified (including a record after the one the caller intends to review)
453	// or mismatched with the supplied checkpoint fail the whole read with
454	// ErrInvalidRange. Failure returns no records. A successful read only
455	// proves the material matches the checkpoint: an original decision that
456	// disagrees with a recomputed one is reported later by offline review, not
457	// treated as archive damage. The result is detached from archive (mutating
458	// one never reaches the other), and the call is read-only.
459	func DecodeAuditArchive(archive []byte, org string, cp Checkpoint) ([]AuditRecord, error) {
460		if org == "" {
461			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
462		}
463		magicLen := len(archiveMagic)
464		if len(archive) < magicLen+4+sha256.Size || string(archive[:magicLen]) != archiveMagic {
465			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unrecognized audit archive", ErrInvalidArchive)
466		}
467		pos := magicLen
468		payloadLen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(archive[pos : pos+4]))
469		pos += 4
470		checksumEnd := pos + payloadLen
471		if payloadLen < 0 || checksumEnd+sha256.Size != len(archive) {
472			// A short frame is truncation; bytes beyond the one frame (a
473			// concatenated second archive, junk appended to a good file) are a
474			// framing failure too.
475			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: truncated or trailing audit archive bytes", ErrInvalidArchive)
476		}
477		payload := archive[pos:checksumEnd]
478		sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
479		if !bytes.Equal(sum[:], archive[checksumEnd:checksumEnd+sha256.Size]) {
480			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checksum mismatch", ErrInvalidArchive)
481		}
482	
483		r := &archiveReader{data: payload}
484		embeddedOrg := r.stringField()
485		embeddedEndSeq := r.u32()
486		embeddedFingerprint := r.stringField()
487		// Every record writes two payload markers, a sequence word, two
488		// fingerprint length words and org/kind length words: 22 bytes even
489		// when every string is empty.
490		n := r.boundedCount(22)
491		if r.err != nil {
492			return nil, r.err
493		}
494		records := make([]AuditRecord, 0, n)
495		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
496			// Read the outer fields in the single record field table's (write
497			// and fingerprint) order, so a field can never be restored into
498			// the wrong member or skipped.
499			var rec AuditRecord
500			for j := range recordFields {
501				f := &recordFields[j]
502				switch f.kind {
503				case recordFieldString:
504					f.setString(&rec, r.stringField())
505				case recordFieldInt:
506					f.setInt(&rec, r.u32())
507				case recordFieldChange:
508					f.setChange(&rec, r.change())
509				case recordFieldDecision:
510					f.setDecision(&rec, r.decisionRecord())
511				}
512			}
513			records = append(records, rec)
514		}
515		if r.err != nil {
516			return nil, r.err
517		}
518		if r.pos != len(payload) {
519			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d unconsumed archive bytes", ErrInvalidArchive, len(payload)-r.pos)
520		}
521	
522		// Content checks reuse the exact audit-range validation the live export
523		// and offline review paths use, so an archive can never smuggle in a
524		// shape those entry points would reject.
525		if embeddedOrg != org {
526			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: archive organization %q does not match %q", ErrInvalidRange, embeddedOrg, org)
527		}
528		// The embedded checkpoint is informational; still, contradicting its own
529		// header means the payload was altered, and the authoritative check
530		// below always uses the caller's independently retained checkpoint.
531		if embeddedEndSeq != cp.EndSeq || embeddedFingerprint != cp.Fingerprint {
532			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: embedded checkpoint does not match the retained checkpoint", ErrInvalidRange)
533		}
534		if err := VerifyAudit(org, records, cp); err != nil {
535			return nil, err
536		}
537		return records, nil
538	}

1	// Command offline_review_example is the end-to-end worked example for
2	// `darksafe review`. It makes one real access decision, saves the complete
3	// audit archive and a separately retained checkpoint, and prints the exact
4	// review command to run next. Everything runs offline in one short program;
5	// after it exits neither the in-memory Store nor the original access request
6	// is needed for the review.
7	//
8	// Run with:
9	//
10	//	go run ./examples/offline_review
11	//
12	// The program takes no arguments. It writes two files into the working
13	// directory:
14	//
15	//   - acme-factory.audit: the complete audit archive, sequence 1 (the
16	//     resource-scoped policy publish) through sequence 2 (the read
17	//     decision), pinned by the independently saved checkpoint.
18	//   - acme-factory.checkpoint: the checkpoint kept SEPARATELY from the
19	//     archive; its end sequence and fingerprint are what a later review
20	//     must pass on the command line.
21	//
22	// Both files are deterministic: the same inputs always produce the same
23	// bytes and fingerprint.
24	package main
25	
26	import (
27		"fmt"
28		"os"
29	
30		"github.com/asdhoaiqqq/darksafe-access/darksafe"
31	)
32	
33	// Archive and checkpoint filenames for the worked example.
34	const (
35		archivePath    = "acme-factory.audit"
36		checkpointPath = "acme-factory.checkpoint"
37	)
38	
39	func main() {
40		if err := run(); err != nil {
41			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "offline review example: failed:", err)
42			os.Exit(1)
43		}
44	}
45	
46	// run contains the whole worked flow. Every error is fatal because the
47	// example exists to show the exact sequence of calls: a skipped or tolerated
48	// failure would leave the user without the materials the printed command
49	// needs.
50	func run() error {
51		// One organization. The name intentionally contains a space: it is
52		// carried verbatim through publish, decision, archive and review, and
53		// must be quoted on the review command line.
54		const org = "acme factory"
55	
56		// One ledger, addressed by both an exact resource id and a scope path.
57		// The policy binds subject + read + scope and then narrows to exactly
58		// this resource id, so the same subject reading another ledger in the
59		// same scope is not authorized by it.
60		const (
61			ledgerID    = "ledger-2026"
62			ledgerScope = "acme/factory/ledger"
63			subjectID   = "svc-audit-reader"
64		)
65	
66		store := darksafe.NewStore()
67	
68		// Publish exactly one allow policy: only svc-audit-reader may read,
69		// within the ledger scope, ledger-2026 and no other resource. Expected
70		// version 0 because nothing has been published for this organization.
71		published, err := store.Publish(org, 0, []darksafe.Policy{
72			{
73				ID:         "p-ledger-read-2026",
74				Subject:    subjectID,
75				Action:     "read",
76				Scope:      ledgerScope,
77				Effect:     darksafe.EffectAllow,
78				ResourceID: ledgerID,
79			},
80		})
81		if err != nil {
82			return fmt.Errorf("publish ledger-read policy as version 1: %w", err)
83		}
84	
85		// Make one real read decision through the organization-level API. Both
86		// organization fields equal the decision organization, the action is
87		// read, and the resource id is the one the policy narrows to.
88		req := darksafe.OrgRequest{
89			SubjectOrg:  org,
90			ResourceOrg: org,
91			Subject: darksafe.Subject{
92				ID:   subjectID,
93				Kind: "service",
94			},
95			Resource: darksafe.Resource{
96				ID:    ledgerID,
97				Scope: ledgerScope,
98			},
99			Action: "read",
100		}
101		decision := store.Decide(org, req)
102		if !decision.Allowed {
103			// The published allow policy matches this exact subject/scope/
104			// resource, so a denial here means the example's own inputs drifted
105			// and the archive must not be saved as "the allowed example".
106			return fmt.Errorf("expected the read to be allowed, got denial: allowed=%v reason=%q matched=%v version=%d",
107				decision.Allowed, decision.Reason, decision.Matched, decision.Version)
108		}
109		fmt.Printf("online decision: allowed=%v reason=%q matched=%v policy version=%d\n",
110			decision.Allowed, decision.Reason, decision.Matched, decision.Version)
111		fmt.Printf("published policy became version %d\n", published)
112	
113		// Export the complete chain (publish record + decision record) and its
114		// pinning checkpoint. AuditExport returns detached copies; when the
115		// Store disappears at the end of run(), these are all that remains.
116		records, cp, err := store.AuditExport(org, 0)
117		if err != nil {
118			return fmt.Errorf("export complete audit chain: %w", err)
119		}
120		if len(records) != 2 {
121			// Guard the narrative: seq 1 must be the publish and seq 2 the
122			// decision; otherwise the printed --seq would point at the wrong
123			// record.
124			return fmt.Errorf("expected 2 audit records (publish + decision), got %d", len(records))
125		}
126		if records[0].Kind != darksafe.AuditPolicyChange || records[1].Kind != darksafe.AuditDecision {
127			return fmt.Errorf("unexpected record kinds: seq1=%q seq2=%q", records[0].Kind, records[1].Kind)
128		}
129		targetSeq := records[1].Seq
130		if targetSeq != 2 {
131			return fmt.Errorf("decision record should be seq 2 (publish occupies seq 1), got %d", targetSeq)
132		}
133	
134		// Encode and save the archive.
135		archive, err := darksafe.EncodeAuditArchive(org, records, cp)
136		if err != nil {
137			return fmt.Errorf("encode audit archive: %w", err)
138		}
139		if err := os.WriteFile(archivePath, archive, 0o600); err != nil {
140			return fmt.Errorf("write archive %s: %w", archivePath, err)
141		}
142	
143		// Save the checkpoint SEPARATELY from the archive. A real retention
144		// scheme keeps it elsewhere (another host, a seal, a paper record); here
145		// it is simply a second file the archive cannot rewrite. The archive
146		// also carries a checkpoint, but it is informational only and can never
147		// stand in for this one.
148		if err := writeCheckpoint(checkpointPath, cp); err != nil {
149			return err
150		}
151	
152		// Report the saved materials and the exact review command to run next.
153		fmt.Println()
154		fmt.Println("materials saved:")
155		fmt.Printf("  archive:    %s (%d bytes, %d records)\n", archivePath, len(archive), len(records))
156		fmt.Printf("  checkpoint: %s  [kept separately]\n", checkpointPath)
157		fmt.Println()
158		fmt.Println("separately retained checkpoint:")
159		fmt.Printf("  org:         %q\n", cp.Org)
160		fmt.Printf("  end-seq:     %d\n", cp.EndSeq)
161		fmt.Printf("  fingerprint: %s\n", cp.Fingerprint)
162		fmt.Println()
163		fmt.Println("Now run (the Store and the original request are gone; the review reads")
164		fmt.Println("only the saved materials and never re-submits the request):")
165		fmt.Println()
166		fmt.Println("  go run ./cmd/darksafe review \\")
167		fmt.Printf("    --archive %s \\\n", archivePath)
168		fmt.Printf("    --org '%s' \\\n", cp.Org)
169		fmt.Printf("    --seq %d \\\n", targetSeq)
170		fmt.Printf("    --end-seq %d \\\n", cp.EndSeq)
171		fmt.Printf("    --fingerprint %s\n", cp.Fingerprint)
172		fmt.Println()
173		fmt.Println("Two ways to pick the wrong material:")
174		fmt.Println()
175		fmt.Printf("  (a) --seq %d instead of %d: it points at the policy publish record,\n", records[0].Seq, targetSeq)
176		fmt.Println("      which is not a decision; review exits 1 with a distinguishable")
177		fmt.Println("      error on stderr and prints nothing on stdout.")
178		fmt.Println()
179		fmt.Println("  (b) a fingerprint that does not match the archive: same exit code 1,")
180		fmt.Println("      same stderr-only, no partial review.")
181		return nil
182	}
183	
184	// writeCheckpoint writes the independently retained checkpoint as small
185	// plain text, so the user can read what they are trusting out-of-band:
186	// one field per line, org quoted byte-for-byte with %q, fingerprint raw.
187	func writeCheckpoint(path string, cp darksafe.Checkpoint) error {
188		content := fmt.Sprintf("org=%q\nend_seq=%d\nfingerprint=%s\n", cp.Org, cp.EndSeq, cp.Fingerprint)
189		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o600); err != nil {
190			return fmt.Errorf("write checkpoint %s: %w", path, err)
191		}
192		return nil
193	}
